title: Rescaled translates of a compactly supported continuous function converge uniformly with a common compact support
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support, let y ∈ ℝ^P, and let c_k ∈ ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) with c_k → 1 (c_k⁻¹ is the real inverse, with 0⁻¹ = 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P such that: (i) f(w − y) = 0 for all w ∉ K; (ii) for all sufficiently large k, f(c_k⁻¹(w − y)) = 0 for all w ∉ K; (iii) f(c_k⁻¹(w − y)) → f(w − y) uniformly in w ∈ ℝ^P as k → ∞.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (y : Euclid P) (mus : ℕ → ℝ), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto mus atTop (𝓝 1) → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ (∀ w ∉ K, f (w - y) = 0) ∧ (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ w ∉ K, f ((mus k)⁻¹ • (w - y)) = 0) ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k w => f ((mus k)⁻¹ • (w - y))) (fun w => f (w - y)) atTop
